subject: Intermittent return-path failures during peak send; edge policy + conntrack suspicion
messages:
From: support@clearpath-tech.com
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: netops-leads@clearpath-health.com
Date: 2026-10-21T17:45:00Z
Subject: Persistent packet loss on return path during sustained telemetry bursts

Hi Mateo,

We're seeing intermittent packet loss that only shows up during our nightly telemetry bursts to Redwood's private deployment (tenant: clearpath-prod). Inbound SYNs and application traffic reach your edge ok, but a large fraction of responses from Redwood instances (TCP RST/FIN and later ACKs) never complete back to our collectors. The pattern started after we ramped pps on Oct 20 and has been reproducible each night since.

Attached are: a short pcap taken at our collector, the edge FW policy we suspect changed last week, and a set of traceroutes showing divergent return paths during the event. Key observations: 
- Traceroute from our collector: consistent hop-list until hop 6, then sporadic 504/ICMP unreachable back from the edge within the same minute.
- PCAP: many SYN/ACKs captured by our collector without subsequent client ACKs; retransmits from our side but no reply from certain backend IP ranges (10.44.8.0/22).

Can you take a look? This is impacting nightly health telemetry and ingestion. Happy to jump on a call.

Attachments: clearpath_peak_capture_20261021.pcap, edge-fw-policy-20261021.txt, traceroutes_20261021.txt

Thanks,
Aarti Rao
Senior Network Ops
ClearPath Health

From: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
To: support@clearpath-tech.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-21T18:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Persistent packet loss on return path during sustained telemetry bursts

Aarti — thanks for the quick data. I pulled the attachments and kicked off a first-pass look. Copying Karikh (infra networking) and Vanessa (Private deployments) to triage.

Immediate asks from our side to accelerate troubleshooting:
1) Can you confirm whether the collector source IPs are covered by the static allowlist we provided (10.44.0.0/16 vs your NATed egress)? If you have NATed egress, please include the public IPs.
2) Can you attach a longer pcap that includes the 3-way handshake plus the moment we see missing ACKs (5–10 seconds either side)?
3) If you can, run tcpdump at one of your collectors with "tcp and host <one-backend-ip>" for one of the affected backend IPs and share.

Initial look at the edge policy you attached: I see a rate-limit-ish match on TCP established flows and a port translation rule that could be hitting ephemeral port exhaustion in mid-burst. We'll also check conntrack and SNAT behavior on our side.

I'll coordinate a 30-min call if we need packet-level pairing; otherwise we'll update here with findings.

—Mateo
Infra Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com, support@clearpath-tech.com
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-21T19:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Persistent packet loss on return path during sustained telemetry bursts

Thanks for the data Aarti, and thanks Mateo for the triage notes. I pulled the pcap and the traceroutes. Early findings / hypotheses: 

1) Asymmetric return path during high-pps: traceroutes show that when loss occurs, return ICMPs appear to hit a different transit peer and we observe ICMP unreachable or RSTs from an intermediate translator. That lines up with selective loss of responses.
2) Conntrack / SNAT port exhaustion: the pcap has many concurrent ephemeral source ports from your collectors. Our edge SNAT pool for that dedicated VLAN recently had a shrink (short-term scale-down) during last week's autoscaler test — it's possible we are exhausting available SNAT slots and dropping state, leading to RSTs or silent drops on return.
3) FW policy counters: the attached policy contains a per-src-rate clause and a lower-than-expected established-flow timeout for TCP sessions. Under high burst load, the edge behavior could prematurely expire state.

Immediate mitigations we propose (non-disruptive to start):
- Increase conntrack_max and ephemeral port pool for the tenant's edge gateway (temporary bump).
- Apply MSS clamp to the customer-facing gateway to reduce fragmentation risk while we verify MTU end-to-end.
- Whitelist explicit collector IPs/public egress and exempt them from per-src-rate limiting.

If these don't remove the spikes we'll schedule a short maintenance window to increase SNAT pool size and run a paired packet capture (we'll capture on-edge and we ask ClearPath to capture on-collector simultaneously).

I'll prepare a playbook and safe rollback steps. Mateo, can you own the config changes and coordinate timing with ClearPath? Vanessa, Marissa — FYI in case any Dedicated autoscaler or VLAN adjustments are required.

Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: support@clearpath-tech.com
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: netops-leads@clearpath-health.com
Date: 2026-10-22T01:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Persistent packet loss on return path during sustained telemetry bursts

Thanks Karthik — that matches our suspicions. Confirmations for your checklist: 
- Our collector egress is NATed through a small set of public IPs: 54.86.120.11, 54.86.120.12. Those IPs were included in the allowlist previously but may have been excluded after a change last week.
- We captured a longer pcap during the 00:30 burst (attached as clearpath_extended_20261022.pcap; also uploaded to the Drive link). The file contains several handshakes where the SYN/SYN-ACK complete from your side but we never see the final ACK — instead our collector retransmits and eventually tears down.
- Traces are consistent with an intermediate translator returning RST when SNAT slots can't be allocated.

We're available for the paired capture. We can also accept a short 10-min maintenance window at 02:30 UTC tonight if that helps you change conntrack or SNAT sizing quickly.

Regards,
Aarti Rao
Senior Network Ops, ClearPath Health

From: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
To: support@clearpath-tech.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-22T14:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Persistent packet loss on return path during sustained telemetry bursts

Update and plan of action:

Thanks for the extended pcap and IP list — that was helpful. We've scheduled the temporary mitigation window for 2026-10-22 02:30–02:45 UTC (marked as tonight in your timezone) to apply the following, minimal-risk changes: 
- conntrack_max: +50% for tenant VLAN (rollback in 10 minutes if metrics degrade)
- ephemeral SNAT pool: grow by 2x (temporary allocation from spare pool)
- firewall: add explicit exceptions for 54.86.120.11/12 and remove them from per-src-rate limiting group
- enable MSS clamp on edge gateway for the tenant (no downtime expected)

During the window we'll run a paired capture (we'll capture on the edge and ask ClearPath to capture at the collector). If that resolves the issue we'll make the conntrack and SNAT pool increases permanent with a follow-up change control. If the problem persists we'll escalate to a scheduled 1‑hour maintenance to enlarge the SNAT pool and, if needed, re-balance transit paths.

I've created a short playbook (JIRA-REDWOOD-1482) and uploaded it to the shared Drive link. We'll post the capture and initial metrics in that ticket thread after the window.

Thanks everyone — see you on the paired-capture if needed.

—Mateo
Infra Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
